title: Wall manifest, major 2 (DRAFT)
description: DRAFT until wave 4 builds it; nothing reads it before then. A feed: what to show and when (a time-anchored schedule of works, each a device-independent presentation master with a mat colour and label text) and default presentation settings. A document with neither scene nor staging is a complete feed, which is what a public channel serves; a wall's manifest is a private feed that may also carry the control layer's scene and staging. The Player composes the mat itself, so works carry a master and a mat colour, not a composed render, and the mat's mode and width are the Player's to decide. Rules a schema cannot state (every referenced work is in works, slots do not overlap, the horizon is whole days) are in .prawduct/artifacts/player-contract.md § Major 2, and a document that breaks one is malformed.

playlist.description: What hangs on the wall: a theme until the rename, a playlist after.

settings.description: Default presentation settings, the first of three layers: the feed's defaults, then (for a home wall) the curator's wall settings, then the viewer's preferences on the device, each later layer overriding key by key. Every key is optional, and a key absent from every layer means the Player's own default. A Player applies a setting where it can and ignores one its display cannot honour.

mode.description: Text on the display itself. none: no text. caption: static for the whole slot, which is all a Frame can do, because its caption is burned into the image before upload. overlay: timed, shown for the overlay's lead and tail with fades. A label on a separate surface is a label output with its own document, not a mode.

none: the work fitted on black. proportional: a mat of the work's own shape, black beyond. full: mat colour to every edge of the screen. The width is never in the feed: a Player that knows its pixel density keeps the inch rule, and one that does not uses a fraction of the screen's shorter side (player-contract.md § Layout).

overlay.description: When an overlay shows within a slot: for its first lead_seconds and its last tail_seconds.

fade_seconds.description: How long an overlay takes to fade in or out.

text_scale.description: A multiplier on the type size the Player computes from its geometry and the viewing distance.

viewing_distance_m.description: How far a viewer stands, a fact about the room. The Player sizes label type from it and its own geometry.

facts.description: Which of a work's label keys a caption or overlay shows, in this order. Empty shows none. A fact a work's label lacks is not shown.

works.description: Every work the schedule, the scene or staging names, keyed by work id. A Player never holds a reference it cannot resolve.

horizon.description: The span the slots cover, a whole number of days. After it ends with no fresh manifest, the Player replays the slots shifted by whole horizons.

slots.description: In time order, not overlapping, inside the horizon. A time no slot covers is dark.

scene.description: Control layer, absent from a channel's feed. A live override, or null. While active it wins over the schedule; when until passes the wall returns to the schedule on its own. until null holds until released.

staging.description: Control layer, absent from a channel's feed. Works to fetch and compose ahead, because a scene is being assembled. Nothing is shown because of this list.

label.description: Label text only. How it is set is the Player's decision. The artist's name crosses whole and in parts, because a work whose artist has no recorded parts has only the whole.

instant.description: RFC 3339 with an offset. The pattern enforces it, because not every validator checks 'format'.

media.description: The presentation master: unmatted, device-independent, long edge capped.

url.description: Where to fetch it: a URI reference, resolved against the manifest's own URL. Today the server serves it at /media/sha256-<hex>; after a Library/Programming split it may name the Library's host, and no Player needs to change. The sha256 is the identity: the Player verifies the bytes against it, so a url that disagrees is caught at download and discarded.
